FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. This formulation is based on Lindane ( CAS No. 58 -89-9 ) a broad spectrum, pesticide. (Gamma Isomer of -HCN having minimum purity of 99.5 percent almost free from Alpha, Beta, Delta, etc, isomers is called Linckme). Lindane wettable ingredient. powders are generally manufactured to contain 6.5 percent Lindane (m/m.) as active

Lindane wettable powders are widely used for control of large number of pests in agriculture, animal and.public health at low rate of application. In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. For the purpose of'deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied-with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules t'or rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rxmnded oft' value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

The material shall be packed in mild steel or tin plate or fibre board containers lined with polyethylene of thickness not less than 0.062 mm. Retail pack up to 1 kg of material shall be packed in polyethylene bag of not less than 0.062 mm thickness, its mouth heatsea]ed and then packed in cardboard carton individually. Carton for packs up to 500 g shall be as given in IS 6604 but carton for 1 kg packs shall be an `E' fluted corrugated board carton of minimum specification 240 gsm duplex board/80 gsm kraft. The general requirement of packaging shall conform to 2 of IS X190 (Part 1) and amendment thereof, if any. 4.2 Marking The container shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information in addition to the information as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder: a) b) c) d)

3 REQUIREMENTS
3.1 3.1.1 Constituents

The material shall consist of Lindane together with suitable carrier(s), stabilizers(s) and other formulant(s).

3.1.2 Lindane employed in the manufacture of the material shall conform to IS 882 with up to date amendments. 3.2 Description The material shall be a fine, free flowing white to off white homogeneous powder, free from visible extraneous matter and hard aggregates. It shall wet readily on mixing with water providing a suspension suitable for use as spray. 3.3 The material shall also requirements given in Table 1. 3.4 Lindane Content comply with the

5 SAMPLING

6.2.2 After conducting the suspensibility test as described in IS 6940 shake vigorously the remaining one tenth suspension including sediment with sufficient acetone. Make the volume to 250 ml with acetone. 6.2.3 Transfer the lfJ ml of solution-quantitatively to a 250 ml separating funnel. Add 100 ml of 2 percent Sodium Chloride solution. Extract theLindane with 3 portions each of 50 ml rz-hexane. Filter the total n-hexane layer through a bed of anhydrous sodium sulphate. Wash Sodium Sulphate twice with 10-15 ml n-hexane. Evaporate the n-hexane on a water bath and dissolve the residue in 5 ml acetone (taken by pipette) and add to it 5 ml internaI standard solution by pipette (see A-1.4.1). Shake well to homogenize. Use this solution for injection in gas chromatographic column as described in A-1.2.1, Lindane contenting sediment where M, RI R, = Mass in .g of Lindane standard solution, in reference in the suspension including = m = M,x R2x PxD R,

When a bulk quantity of the material is offered for inspection, representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 10627 and tested within 90 days of its manufacturing. The criteria for conformity shall be as given in IS 10627. When the material "is offered for inspection after 90 days of its manufacturing sampling shall be done according to IS 10627 and the criteria for conformity shall be as given in IS 10627. However, the criteria for conformity of the material when tested shall be the limit of tolerances, as applicable over the declared nominal value given under 3.4 of this standard. 6 TESTS

METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF CONTENT IN LINDANE WETTABLE

A-O General Lindane content is determined by gas liquid chromatography by using an internal standard and a flame ionization detector. A-1 GAS CHROMATOGRAPHIC METHOD

A-1.3.2 A-1.3.3

Lindane standard of known purity. Internal Standard

Alpha naphthol. A-1.4 Preparation
Solutions A-1.4.1 of Standard and Sample

A-1.l Gas liquid chromatography fitted with a flame ionization detector (FID) is used for lindane content determination. Using -solution containing known amounts of the standard Lindane and internal standard the response factor R for Lindane content and internal standard is arrived at a solu(ion containing a known mass of sample and internal standard is injected into theGLC unit. The percentage of Lindane content is then computed. A-1.2 Apparatus
A-1.2.1
Gas

Preparation

of Internal Standard Solution

Weigh accurately about 150 mg of internal standard into a 100 ml volume with glass stopper. Add by pipette 10ml of internal standard solution and 10 ml acetone. Stopper the flask, tightly and gently swirl the contents for one minute using a rotational motion of the wrist. Allow to stand for at least five minutes and then shake for one minute. Centrifuge the above solution in a stoppered tube and use supernatant layer as sample solution for injection in gas chromatographic column. A-1.5 Estimation A-1.5.1 operating Conditions Operating conditions for gas liquid chromatography: The temperatures, gas flow rates and retention times given below are typical values and may have to be adjusted to obtain optimum results from a given apparatus. Gas Flow Carrier Gas (Nitrogen) Fuel Gas (Hydrogen Air Tempemture Column Oven Injection Port .Detector Chart Speed Injection Size 3 160'C 220'C 240"C 0.5 cm/min 2 micro Iitre 25 ml/min 30 ml/min 300 ml/min

Liquid Ck-omatogruph

The instrument should be one that is designed for use with glass columns and that is equipped with an oncolumn injection system and a high-sensitivity flame ionization detector. The suggested parameters aregiven in the operating conditions (A-1.5.1) which can be changed depending upon the available equipment and allied facilities provided standardization is done. Chromatographic column: The column should be a borosilicate glass tube 183 cm length and 4 mm internal dia. packed with 5 percent OV-210 on chromosorb W-HP (100- 120 mesh) or suitable equivalent, bent to fit the chromatography. A-1.2.2 Microsyringe

10 micro litre capacity A-1.3 Reagents
A-1.3.1

Acetone

Analytical reagent grade.
